_about: 737-400, from Boeing D6-58325-6 Rev E (November 2023) 2.2.5 (page index 33): side, plan and front views on one sheet, drawn 1.3% smaller than the 737-300's. Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 14, line centres (side_all.png: fills and the blue strokes together). The 737-300's points moved by the two plugs (plug.py: 1.82 m ahead of the wing, 1.23 m behind it), then snapped. The cabin windows are drawn.

sources.title: Boeing, 737-100/-200/-300/-400/-500 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58325-6 Rev E, November 2023), 2.2.5 General Dimensions: Model 737-400
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b734/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The 737-300's points moved by the fuselage plugs, then snapped onto this sheet. Plain wing tips, as the sheet draws them. The sheet draws the cabin windows; the one behind the wing's line in the drawing is placed at its own position. The side view draws the fuselage 3.95 m tall (line centres) where the sheet prints 4.01 m and the front view draws 3.99 m, so the shape is fit to the printed height (fit_height.py). The side view draws the engine's inlet lip 12.14 m from the nose and the plan view 12.83 m; the sheet prints 12.55 m (the 737-300, -400 and -500 sheets all draw the plan's nacelle 0.69 m further back than the side's). The nacelle is moved 0.41 m back to the printed figure (build.py, as for any inlet more than 1.5% off); the wing stays where the plan draws it. Confidence medium for the views' disagreement.
